# Installment 7 / issue #11 — initial independent content review

## Snapshot

- Baseline HEAD: `cbdfd15ef7520624ea8cf748f601842157250a79`, independently verified.
- Included uncommitted content: the four files in `[review workspace]\n5-giving-initial-content`.
- Snapshot specification: adjacent `n5-giving-initial-review-snapshot.json`.
- Review and source retrieval date: 2026-10-22. This is the initial report, to be retained unchanged for reconciliation.

All requested SHA-256 values were independently recomputed with CRLF normalized to LF:

The frozen article, exercise set and source ledger were also byte-identical to their respective live repository files. All 36 frozen vocabulary records exactly equaled the corresponding ordered live inventory records. These checks passed again near completion.

## Scope and reviewer

Reviewer: GitHub Copilot, acting as the independent content reviewer in this session. **The actual runtime model ID was not exposed to this reviewer.** It is not inferred from the author's inventory attribution, defaults or a model-family guess. No delegation was used.

Scope: the complete article; all 36 exercises, including every field, accepted answer, base/additional option, rationale and lexical payload; all set/group metadata; the complete new source ledger, including qualifications, three coverage anchors, six relevant primary entries, required-task mappings and 36 task records; and all 36 complete vocabulary inventory records.

The review assessed ordinary basic transfers, actual giver/receiver roles, narrator/adopted viewpoint, predicate-specific case marking, requested ordinary past forms, matched interpretation and contextual expression. Benefactive auxiliaries, a full honorific system and the optional standpoint/beneficiary bridges were treated as boundaries, not missing N5 targets.

No prior review verdict was used as evidence. No earlier review/reconciliation report or author research, generator or planning artifact was consulted. The new source ledger and author-attributed lexical records were checked as provenance claims, not accepted as review conclusions. `n5-giving-baseline.json` was used only for preservation comparisons.

## Verdicts

| Component | Correctness | Scoped coverage | Comprehensibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Complete learner article | **CLEAN** | **CLEAN** | **CLEAN** |
| Complete 36-exercise/lexical set, including its groups and supporting source/inventory bindings | **CLEAN** | **CLEAN** | **CLEAN** |

**CLEAN means no actionable defect was established within this assigned scope, not exhaustive truth or certification.** No consequential unresolved claim was identified.

## Findings

**None: 0 actionable findings; no severity assigned.**

### Basis for the verdicts

- **Article:** The opening cookie transfer is correctly described through giver-subject くれる and receiver-topic もらう. Subsequent examples preserve those roles, distinguish human-source に／から from recipient に, and explicitly avoid treating every は as a subject marker. Giving within a family, receiving from relatives and adopted third-person viewpoint are explained without permanent family partitions. Ordinary plain/polite past formation is productive and correct, including もらった versus もらいました. Readings, translations and the linked foundations support the stated entry-level task.
- **Formation and marking:** All 12 verb-form tasks visibly name the verb and requested past/register form. All eight marker tasks visibly bound the case-particle operation; the subject tasks exclude a different source/topic framing. Both human-source tasks accept に and から, and each supplies the second form as an additional correct option. The actual wrong completions and feedback were checked, including double-object and changed-role cases.
- **Interpretation:** All eight tasks correctly identify the requested giver or receiver. 前者／後者 are defined, read and ordered consistently before answering, independent of the correct label. Feedback rejects the selected wrong role rather than affirming it. The cookie and ticket descriptions preserve their matched events and context keys.
- **Contextual expression:** All eight tasks state the event, narrator and required form. The two third-person viewpoint selections make the requested perspective explicit; feedback distinguishes another grammatical framing from the requested one instead of inventing a universal prohibition. Replacing the verb with もらう is correctly assessed against the printed participant roles. No inferred gratitude, happiness or intention is added to the factual transfer.
- **Accepted forms and lexical support:** Every literal completion was examined, not merely the answer IDs. The 66 accepted strings fit their visible tasks; the corresponding 上げる／呉れる／貰う forms are retained without importing unrelated homophones. The 108 lexical spans have fitting local readings, headwords and senses; the 188 exclusions protect the task and cover the remaining prompt text. No canonical word-card identity is asserted by the payloads.
- **Coverage and provenance:** All four groups and 11 facets match their owned exercises. Every facet has at least two distinct context keys. The three recommendations are soft links, with no hard prerequisites. The 11 key strings correctly account for reused or paired events rather than claiming 36 independent conversations. All 36 source task records and relationship-level mappings agree with the exercises. The six inspected primary lessons support the required grammar, not an inference from vocabulary difficulty or an official JLPT syllabus.

## Independently inspected source evidence

The actual Bunpro main lessons were inspected, including Structure, About, relevant Related material and all five public examples for each of the six entries. Forum replies were not used as linguistic evidence. Simplified extraction omitted Japanese on some pages; direct HTML text extraction restored it before the relevant claims were assessed.

| Actual source | Evidence relevant to this review |
| --- | --- |
| [Bunpro あげる](https://bunpro.jp/grammar_points/あげる) | N5 basic-transfer frame; giver は／が, recipient に, object を. Its younger-brother example directly supports giving within a family. |
| [Bunpro くれる](https://bunpro.jp/grammar_points/くれる) | N5 giver/recipient frame; mother, brother and grandfather giving to the speaker, plus a friend giving to the speaker's mother. Those actual examples prevent a fixed-family reading of the broader group shorthand. |
| [Bunpro もらう](https://bunpro.jp/grammar_points/もらう) | N5 receiver-centered frame and actual に／から human-source examples. The related auxiliary lesson is distinct from basic transfer. |
| [Bunpro godan past](https://bunpro.jp/grammar_points/う-verb-past) | N5 ordinary past formation, including う → った and the distinct i-row polite stem. |
| [Bunpro ichidan past](https://bunpro.jp/grammar_points/る-verb-past) | N5 removal of る before た／ました; paired plain/polite examples. |
| [Bunpro polite endings](https://bunpro.jp/grammar_points/polite-verb-endings) | N5 stem + ます; ending politeness is not an unrestricted honorific-verb rule. |
| [Tae Kim, giving and receiving](https://www.guidetojapanese.org/favor.html) | Actual Japanese third-person giver/receiver-viewpoint examples, both source particles, and the explicit receiving-from-the-speaker qualification. Read with inline Japanese restored. |
| [Wasabi, giving and receiving](https://wasabi-jpn.com/magazine/japanese-grammar/receiving-and-giving/) | Basic role tables, giving to one's mother, receiving from her, and mother receiving from the speaker. Its absolute third-party/group and guaranteed-happiness claims were not adopted. |

Fresh JMdict/Jisho inspection covered the exact transfer senses and competing same-reading entries:

- [あげる](https://jisho.org/api/v1/search/words?keyword=あげる): 上げる, giving sense 5, ichidan/transitive and usually kana; separate 揚げる and 挙げる do not supply that gift-transfer sense. The appended Wikipedia deep-frying material is not evidence for giving.
- [くれる](https://jisho.org/api/v1/search/words?keyword=くれる): 呉れる sense 1, its speaker/close-person qualification and special ichidan class; the separate disdainful sense supports the task's ordinary-neutral boundary. 暮れる and its spellings are different lexical material.
- [もらう](https://jisho.org/api/v1/search/words?keyword=もらう): 貰う sense 1 and godan-う class; auxiliary, victory and disease senses are separate.

Actual dictionary entries were also freshly retrieved for 私／わたし, 妹／いもうと, 本／ほん, 友達／ともだち, 切符／きっぷ, 母／はは, クッキー, 兄／あに, ノート, 先生／せんせい, 地図／ちず, 絵はがき／えはがき, 花／はな, 前者／ぜんしゃ and 後者／こうしゃ. The gift context selects the food-cookie and physical-notebook senses. Fictional surname readings 田中／たなか and 山田／やまだ are locally specified, not claims about every bearer of those names. Dictionary vocabulary-level tags were not used to grade grammar.
